subject: Backup purge interlock and subprocessor dataflow — clarification for DPA
messages:
From: Tara Benton <tara.benton@novamed.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: support@novamed.com
Date: 2027-09-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify backup purge timing and subprocessor transfers — NovaMed DPA

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the call yesterday. We need to close a few open items in the DPA before the procurement team signs off:

- Primary ask: what is Redwood's end-to-end timeline after a customer requests full data deletion? Specifically: live deletion latency, backup purge job cadence (weekly/daily), and final physical deletion from subprocessor systems.
- Subprocessor detail: you listed "BackupWorks" during the demo — can you confirm their role (hot backups vs. archival), where backups are stored (region), and whether backups cross borders?
- Evidence: we need SOC2, an export proving deletion, and a statement about any log retention that could include customer data.

Attached is our current DPA redline (high level). Can we get a short written summary and a suggested amendment clause we can present to our legal/compliance team? If possible, please copy your security lead.

Also would like a short call next week with Redwood + BackupWorks + NovaMed legal to confirm the operational flow.

Thanks,
Tara Benton
Legal Ops — NovaMed

Attachments referenced: nova_med_dpa_redlines.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tara Benton <tara.benton@novamed.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-29T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify backup purge timing and subprocessor transfers — NovaMed DPA

Tara — thanks for the clear list. I pulled the team together and summarized below; happy to hop on a call with BackupWorks and your legal team. Proposed times in a follow-up.

Short written summary (current behavior):
- Live data deletion: initiated by request -> internal job marks account flagged for deletion within 24–48 hours; active data removed from primary stores within 48 hours.
- Backup purge cadence: incremental backup snapshots are retained per our retention tiering; BackupWorks runs a weekly purge job that marks snapshots for deletion. Final object removal from backup storage (garbage collection cycle) depends on storage tier: warm backups ~60 days, cold/archival ~365 days.
- Cross-border storage: BackupWorks maintains replicated copies in us-central and eu-west; copy location depends on region setting and SSO configuration.
- Log retention: system telemetry (aggregated) retained 90 days by default; audit logs are longer (up to 24 months) but we redact PII from telemetry.

Suggested DPA amendment language (draft):
- Redwood will ensure the following for NovaMed: live data removal within 48 hours of request; backup snapshots containing unique customer content will be purged from primary backup tiers within 45 days except where required for legal hold; final physical object deletion from all subprocessor systems will be completed within 90 days of purge initiation. Redwood will provide a deletion attestation within 14 days of final removal.

Notes/risks:
- Forensic/incident holds will pause purge timelines; we recommend an explicit exception flow and an SLA for hold release.
- Shortening warm backup windows to <45 days is achievable with BackupWorks, but cold archive retention (365d) requires contractual amendments with them.

I've attached a retention_matrix_v2.xlsx and will request an evidence pack from BackupWorks (expected within 24 hours).

Action items:
1) Internal: Kimberly will produce the security redline for the subprocessor clause.
2) Internal: Aditya will draft the DPA amendment for DocuSign.
3) Coordination: Ben will coordinate a 30-min working session with NovaMed + BackupWorks.

— Soojin
VP, Solutions & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Anne Cho <anne.cho@backupworks.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Tara Benton <tara.benton@novamed.com>
Date: 2027-09-30T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify backup purge timing and subprocessor transfers — NovaMed DPA

Hi Soojin / Tara — following up from our onboarding notes. Quick vendor-side facts:

- Role: BackupWorks provides encrypted snapshot backups for Redwood; warm snapshots are stored in block-storage object pools, cold snapshots are tiered to long-term object storage.
- Regions: primary copies in us-central; geo-replicas in eu-west on request. For NovaMed we currently have geo-replication enabled (us-central + eu-west).
- Purge mechanics: we tag snapshots for deletion during the weekly GC job; objects become eligible for final removal after the retention TTL expires. For warm snapshots that TTL is currently set to 60d; we can contractually reduce to 30d for a named customer with an SLA change.
- Cross-border: backups are encrypted in transit and at-rest; replication to eu-west is triggered by the region flag. We can commit to keeping EU replicas in eu-west only upon request but need a 14-day transition window to migrate existing objects.
- Evidence: attaching our SOC2 summary and recent deletion logs bundle (see backupworks_evidence_20270927.zip).

If Redwood wants backup final deletion within 45d, we can support that for warm snapshots as long as Redwood updates the retention TTL and we accept the SLA. Cold archive deletion (365d) is deeper and will need a separate addendum.

Happy to discuss on a call.

— Anne Cho
Head of Operations, BackupWorks

Attachments referenced: backupworks_evidence_20270927.zip

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-30T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft language for subprocessor and purge timelines

Soojin / Aditya — I drafted a concise security redline for the DPA that addresses NovaMed's asks and vendor constraints. Key points:

- Proposed commitment: live deletion within 48h; backup warm-tier final deletion within 45 days; return of deletion attestation within 14 days of final object removal.
- Forensics/legal hold: Redwood will notify NovaMed within 24h of any hold request and provide an estimated hold release timeline; purge resumes within 7 days of hold removal.
- Cross-border constraint: If NovaMed requires EU-only backups, Redwood will coordinate a 14-day migration window with BackupWorks and will flag the account for EU-isolation during the transition.
- Audit evidence: Redwood will provide a combined vendor log package (Redwood + BackupWorks) within 14 days of request; logs will include object IDs and deletion job manifests but will exclude service-level internal identifiers.

I added inline redlines in the PDF (link below) — Aditya, please fold these into the DPA amendment.

Related: retention_matrix_v2.xlsx includes proposed TTLs for warm/cold/logs.

— Kimberly
Head of Security Engineering

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tara Benton <tara.benton@novamed.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Anne Cho <anne.cho@backupworks.io>
Date: 2027-10-01T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Backup purge interlock and subprocessor dataflow — consolidated proposal + next steps

Tara — thank you. We've consolidated a short proposal based on the vendor capabilities and our security review. Summary of commitments Redwood proposes for NovaMed:

1) Live deletion: Redwood will remove active customer content within 48 hours of a deletion request.
2) Backup warm-tier: final object deletion within 45 days of purge mark; Redwood will provide a deletion attestation within 14 days of final removal.
3) Cold/archival tier: default 365 days; can be shortened with a BackupWorks addendum.
4) Log retention: audit logs (non-PII) retained up to 24 months; any logs containing customer content will be treated as data subject to deletion requests and will be purged per the retention_matrix_v2.xlsx timelines.
5) Cross-border handling: if NovaMed requires EU-only backups, Redwood + BackupWorks will perform a 14-day migration and prevent new EU replicas creation until migration completes.

Proposed operational steps:
- Ben to schedule a 30-minute working session (Redwood + BackupWorks + NovaMed legal).
- Aditya will upload the DPA amendment to DocuSign (link below) for signature after NovaMed review.
- Kimberley [sic] will provide the security redline as an attachment to the amendment.

Attachments: retention_matrix_v2.xlsx, nova_med_dpa_redlines.pdf
DocuSign draft: https://docusign.redwoodinference.com/envelopes/0X7A9F-clause-amendment

Please let us know if the 45-day warm-tier commitment is acceptable; if yes we'll proceed to update the DPA and the subprocessor addendum.

Regards,
Soojin
VP, Solutions & Partnerships
